text: {"frames":["\"Hold the lantern up,\" said Femke, and she did not say another word. The blue lamp on her barge had gone out at dusk, but now it burned again and drifted ahead of us over the black canal. It led us along {a} cells of the plan, then {b} more past the herring stall, and {c|cell|cells|cells} more to the mill where the light always goes out. Every cell of the plan is {d} m on the ground. How many metres long is the route that the blue lantern showed us?","Thijs the lock keeper found his brass whistle gone from its hook at dawn. Behind the cupboard in the lock house, someone was humming an old song, very softly and very out of tune. He followed the humming along the wet path, {a} cells of the plan, then {b} more over the little bridge, and {c|cell|cells|cells} more to the dripping cellar door. Each cell of the plan is {d} m on the ground. How many metres did Thijs walk from his hook to the humming?","I lifted the lid of the cheese crate, and faraway music rose out of it like steam. The cellar smelled of old cheese and cold stone, and the tune pulled me down a narrow canal between the rounds. The path went {a} cells of the plan under the arches, then {b} more beside the drying racks, and {c|cell|cells|cells} more to the bottom of the stairs. Every cell of the plan is {d} m on the ground. How many metres of cellar did the music lead me along?","The smell of wet rope and cold tar filled the lock house before anything else. Down in the chamber the water rose and fell, slowly, as if something under the gate was breathing. Isa the cat sat on the rail and counted her steps aloud, because she had gone along this route in the night. She had walked {a} cells of the plan to the sluice, then {b} more along the top of the dyke, and {c|cell|cells|cells} more down to the water. Each cell of the plan is {d} m on the ground. How many metres did Isa walk tonight?","All the windows of the crooked house with the hoist beam were lit, though nobody lived there. Luuk, the keeper of forgotten things, stood below with a lamp and a list in his coat. The light had sent a trail of footprints in the frost, and he meant to follow them to the source. The trail ran {a} cells of the plan past the tulip field, then {b} more over the ice, and {c|cell|cells|cells} more to the lit door. Every cell of the plan is {d} m on the ground. How many metres long is the trail of footprints that Luuk must follow?"]}
